title: Rama spares the spies
hook: two spies dressed as monkeys are caught in Rama's camp, and he lets them go unharmed
carry: maryada: dharma keeps its limits in war

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vibhishana's crossing. Rama vowed safety to anyone who comes even once and says I am yours, and crowned Vibhishana on the beach. Sharanagati: whoever comes once is held.

The army crosses the bridge and spreads out along Lanka's shore. Across the island, Ravana does what any general would. He sends two of his ministers, Shuka and Sarana, to count the enemy. They take the shape of monkeys and slip in among the troops. It almost works. But one person in that camp knows exactly what a rakshasa in disguise looks like, because he grew up among them. Vibhishana sees through them, and they're dragged before Rama.
screen: `THE ARMY IS ACROSS.` → `TWO SPIES DRESSED AS MONKEYS.` → `VIBHISHANA SEES THROUGH THEM.`

segments.voice: In a war story, you know what usually happens to caught spies, and the monkeys are ready to do it. The two rakshasas, terrified, confess: Ravana sent us to count your army. And Rama laughs. If you've seen everything, he says, go back. If you missed anything, look again; Vibhishana will show you around. You're unarmed and you were caught. You won't be killed. Then he hands them a message for Ravana: show me the strength you relied on when you carried Sita away. The spies go home, name Rama's leaders one by one from Ravana's tower, and end with advice he doesn't want: make peace and return Sita. Ravana throws them out. Hindus have a name for Rama that this scene shows: maryada purushottam, the best of men, who keeps the bounds of dharma. Maryada means a boundary. Rama has every reason to be cruel here: it's war, his wife is a captive, the enemy is spying on him. And still there's a line he won't cross. Hindu teaching calls this dharma yuddha, righteous war, and the Mahabharata sets out such rules before its own great battle: you don't strike the unarmed, or someone who can't fight back. Rama isn't soft. His message is a hard one. But winning doesn't move the line. Today, the spies are more likely to be screenshots. When you've caught someone in the wrong and could make an example of them, maryada asks one question: is this something a person of dharma does, even when they could?
screen: `CAUGHT SPIES, AND A LAUGH.` · `LOOK AGAIN, THEN GO HOME.` · `MARYADA: A BOUNDARY.` · `DHARMA YUDDHA: RIGHTEOUS WAR.` · then, large: `WINNING DOESN'T MOVE THE LINE.`

segments.voice: Many Hindu homes light a small lamp at the family shrine in the evening. Sit before a lamp, or any small light, and fold your hands. Bring to mind someone you're angry with, someone you could hurt if you wanted to. Breathe slowly, and say to Rama, silently, one line you won't cross with them, however the fight goes. Then bow your head. If you don't pray, simply sit with the light and name the line.
The siege. It begins with two spies caught and set free, unharmed, carrying a hard message, because even in war Rama keeps the bounds of dharma.
Your line: maryada, dharma keeps its limits in war. Next, one last offer at the gates. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 639 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: WHY TALK WHEN THE CITY IS SURROUNDED?`

howItsDone: Storytellers often use the release of Shuka and Sarana to show the code of war in the Ramayana: an unarmed messenger or captive is not killed.

fork.reveal: Rama caught the spies red-handed and still sent them home unharmed. maryada: some things a person of dharma doesn't do, even when he could.

original.note: Sanskrit maryādā: a boundary or limit; Rama is called Maryādā Puruṣottama, the best of men, who keeps the bounds of dharma.

trapdoor: what you thought: Rama let the spies go because he was just being nice.
what it means: it's maryada: even at war, with every reason to be cruel, Rama won't harm the unarmed and the captured.
what a scholar hears: Hindu teaching on dharma yuddha, righteous war, limits who may be struck; the Mahabharata lays out such rules before Kurukshetra.

Shuka.meaning: one of Ravana's ministers, sent to spy on Rama's army

Sarana.meaning: Ravana's minister who names Rama's leaders from the tower

rakshasa.meaning: one of Ravana's people in the epic, able to change shape

Vibhishana.meaning: Ravana's brother, who came over to Rama's side

maryada.meaning: a boundary; keeping the limits of dharma
